item.title: ASP.NET MVC: Generating DropDownLists from Enums
item.description:
“ASP.NET MVC: Generating DropDownLists from Enums”

Generating DropDown Lists from Enums in ASP.NET MVC

Creating a dropdown list from an enumeration involves mapping each enum member to a selectable item. This process can be achieved through several methods, each offering different levels of customization and convenience.

Solution 1: Using Html.EnumDropDownListFor (MVC 5.1 and later)

For ASP.NET MVC 5.1 and newer versions, a built-in helper Html.EnumDropDownListFor simplifies this task significantly.

// In your Model
public enum TaskStatus
{
    Pending,
    InProgress,
    Completed,
    Cancelled
}

// In your View
@Html.EnumDropDownListFor(model => model.CurrentStatus, "Select a Status", new { @class = "form-control" })

If you wish to use descriptive text for enum members, you can employ the [Display] attribute, which Html.EnumDropDownListFor respects in MVC 5.1+.

item.title: Effective Methods for AJAX File Downloads in Web Applications
item.description:
“Effective Methods for AJAX File Downloads in Web Applications”

This discussion outlines several proven strategies, ranging from using temporary server storage like TempData to serving files directly from memory streams.

Core Challenge: Serving Files Post-AJAX Request

The fundamental constraint is that an AJAX call is designed for data exchange, not for triggering a browser’s download mechanism directly upon completion. Therefore, the solution requires a two-step process:

  1. Client Action: AJAX post submits parameters to the server.
  2. Server Response & Client Redirection: The server generates the file content (or a reference to it) and sends back a response that instructs the browser to navigate to a separate download endpoint.

Solutions

Strategy 1: Using TempData for In-Memory File Handling (Recommended for MVC)

This approach avoids creating physical files on the server, relying instead on ASP.NET MVC’s TempData to temporarily hold the file’s byte array between requests. TempData is typically backed by Session but is automatically cleared after the subsequent request, offering better memory efficiency than relying solely on Session for high-volume exports.

item.description:
“Solved: How to Bind Form Controls to a Model in MVC using Foreach Loops and Editor Templates”

Q: Why do my form inputs not bind to my model properties when using a foreach loop in MVC

ANS: When using a foreach loop in your ASP.NET MVC views, the HTML name attributes for your form controls are typically generated as item.PropertyName (e.g., <input type="text" name="item.LeaveType" />). For model binding to work correctly on postback, these name attributes must precisely match the expected structure of your model, including collection indices. This means they should look like CollectionName[index].PropertyName (e.g., <input type="text" name="LeaveDetailsList[0].LeaveType" />). Without this specific naming convention, the default binder cannot correctly associate the submitted values with the corresponding properties in your model’s collection.
